summary: A guide published for Mental Health Awareness Month (October 2023) that uses stories of young people to illustrate how to navigate mental health services. It covers acknowledging the need, exploring therapy and community options, funding and insurance, building support systems, self-advocacy, education, e-mental health tools, sharing stories, and youth-friendly institutional changes.
one_line: A guide using stories of teens to show how to find, fund, and advocate for mental health services, written for Mental Health Awareness Month 2023.
key_facts: Emma Jacobs, 17, confided in a teacher about her anxiety on September 12, 2023, and was directed to school counselor Mrs. Linda Green.
Emma Jacobs chose therapy and found that cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) resonated with her coping style.
David Nguyen, 17, explored local community groups on October 3, 2023, and supplemented group sessions with mindfulness practices.
Marcus Brown, 16, consulted his family and a social worker on September 18, 2023, and learned his family's health insurance covered online counseling sessions.
A public awareness campaign on September 25, 2023, highlighted sliding scale services and programs for people without comprehensive insurance.
Jenna Kim, 18, shared her experiences with a local peer support group on her social media platform on October 10, 2023, and got overwhelmingly positive reactions.
Anthony Wallace, 15, found immense support from his siblings after opening up to them on October 15, 2023.
Sarah Martin, 19, felt dismissed at a mental health appointment on October 20, 2023, and sought a second opinion to advocate for her needs.
Alex Johnson attended a seminar on mental health literacy at his high school on September 29, 2023.
Mia Chen began using an app for meditation and mood tracking on October 5, 2023, as an example of e-mental health services.
Nicolas Garcia shared his story of dealing with depression on his blog on November 1, 2023.
Dr. Rachel Stevenson and her team at the local clinic revamped their approach to make mental health services more youth-friendly on September 27, 2023.
